notes: The same genetically integrated corolla-shape system changes bumblebee attraction and ant-predation risk in opposing directions; tubular manipulation reduces predation but also pollen receipt and seed set.
Bite force and jaw-closing velocity are negatively correlated within and among species; the same jaw apparatus constrains feeding performance and song-related gape modulation.

Paired claws are initially equivalent and experimental rearing or differential exercise can direct which homolog becomes crusher versus cutter; the function-separating developmental route is experimentally manipulable.
Adult crusher-versus-cutter mechanics document specialization after the split and therefore cannot by themselves establish coupling in the pre-split shared state.
The existence of feeding and pollinating anthers is the focal structural outcome; it cannot also serve as independent evidence that heteranthery was accessible before the split.

Pollen simultaneously functions as gamete and pollinator food and the paper explicitly frames this as an evolutionary conflict; independence from the differentiated anther outcome still requires a pre-heteranthery or homantherous comparator audit.
Mutational paths that increase TrpF-like activity commonly reduce or eliminate ancestral HisA activity in the same protein sequence; direct integrated-state trade-off evidence.

A separate experimental-evolution study generated duplication-and-divergence in the HisA/TrpF system, suggesting a function-separating route is accessible; context dependence and duplicate macro rows must be audited before adjudication.

Single-copy and experimentally constructed two-active-copy populations were both evolved before observing whether copies specialized; duplication was therefore an ex ante available architecture rather than inferred from the outcome.
Improving green fluorescence trades off with blue fluorescence in the same coGFP sequence; direct shared-sequence performance conflict.
Observed production of male-only flowers is the resolution outcome and cannot itself establish prior architectural accessibility.

Within bisexual flowers strong protogyny couples female-first function to delayed male function and measured male-versus-female selection on pistil number and flowering time reveals the conflict before using male-only flowers as explanatory evidence.
The ancestral single GAL gene is bifunctional and precise replacements identify an adaptive regulatory conflict between galactokinase and coinduction requirements.
The historical GAL1/GAL3 duplication is the focal resolution outcome and cannot be reused as an independent accessibility predictor without a separate pre-outcome route estimate.
A single shared beak being observed today does not demonstrate that function-separating architectures were historically inaccessible.
